how: Proposing a flag and reporting its first placement instantiate starting separately from the subsequent member commitment.
The revised role's call-based explanation of joining needs a local bound because the immediate answer follows a report of placement.
Members propose waiting for more helpers and making a fresh announcement, without documenting an agreed start hour.
Anticipating being overrun with only two participants makes waiting for more people relevant before building.
A reported first pixel receives a bare commitment to join.
The bare join immediately answers a placement report, so an explicit call cannot be treated as the only direct route to commitment.
A visible start receives a joining response, supplementing the call-to-answer route without establishing an obligation for every reader.
The question about whether the flag was achieved receives an assessment that flag hearts were the best surviving result.
Concern about being overrun and laughter about the outcome do not establish withdrawal under stress or repair of an interpersonal quarrel.
Members settle workable pixel proportions and defer room for the quetzal to later enlargement.
First-pixel and left-edge announcements report the state and location of work already begun.

Recruitment recurs after construction starts, so an unrepeated call-before-building sequence cannot account for the requested publicity.
Reporting that placement has begun prompts a request to announce the start to the room.
Requested publicity after the first placement makes the start visible and returns its announcement to the earlier planning branch.
Verbal pixel dimensions and explicit acceptance settle the observed design exchange without requiring a subsequently posted template.
Informal-looking replies cannot establish whether leadership, votes, or divisions of work were decided elsewhere or validate a population claim.
The repair recollection does not identify scripts, bots, spare accounts, or manual placement as its means.

Public coordinates, return links, and a takeover title do not establish concealment, infiltration, or disguised scripts.
Proposed synchronization seeks more helpers without identifying sleep, work, travel, devices, or personal placing costs.
Acknowledging closure does not establish site faults, timer glitches, or technical workarounds.

The added keeper-knowledge mechanism cannot be tested because no passage connects an agreed design change to repairs that erased it.
The flag's first-pixel report and the heart's retrospective repairs lack established mark continuity and repair times.
Naming the Lakers as taking a heart reports attribution without showing investigation of placers or motives.
The repair report supplies no observed escalation from upkeep under attack to machine placements.
The proposed spot beneath a neighbouring flag and a similar size instantiate choosing space before any recorded loss.
A speaker protecting the Kuwait flag asks the takeover caller to migrate and points to other available hearts.
Own-room restraint requires affiliation evidence because this reasoned objection identifies with the threatened work rather than demonstrably policing the attacking room.
Loss and survival reports do not establish a decision to relocate, its execution, or continuity between the flag and the surviving heart.
The early judgment of too few hands cannot be linked to a documented later relocation.
The migration plea does not document settled borders, a truce, or an agreement.
Using a neighbouring flag as a landmark and asking a caller to move do not establish exchanged help.
The location offer and objection provide no observed coalition or shared organizing body.
Claiming an occupied flag does not establish guests building under a host's rules.

The broadened standing entry remains unobserved because the plea concerns location rather than limits on committing other placers.
Neither an agreement nor a subsequent dispute over binding a room appears in the surviving takeover exchange.

Identification with the threatened flag does not establish dual membership or torn allegiance.
Flag proportions and a planned quetzal do not establish national history, politics, lore, or colour doctrine beyond the mark.
The surviving title justifies taking a heart through the target's three hearts, while the deleted body leaves prior quarrels unresolved.
Naming a national target does not establish a pre-existing tie that names the rival as the reason for attacking.
Laughter in a loss assessment is insufficient to identify a new canvas joke or its uptake.
The flag proposal and announcement do not establish a new room formed around a canvas mark.
The plea concerns occupied space without an observed dispute about offensive language, jokes, or hate symbols.
The actionable proposal and first-pixel report do not establish room-wide April Fools framing or a fake call.
Requested announcements and return links show publicity without observed host rules or containment of canvas talk.
Recruitment is visible, but a canvas flood and a resulting host boundary remain unobserved.
A call to take another group's heart does not show hostility to the room's own canvas posts or mark.
Participants report a lost heart, assess flag hearts as the best result, and locate a survivor after closure.
The surviving-heart announcement and retrospective repair answer mark the result and a member's contribution.
Announcements of early pixels and a later surviving heart cannot establish a finished-mark report causing collective celebration of that same mark.

Closing reports preserve the result without an observed decision to continue through another canvas, emblem, or organization.
The outcome account has no observed continuation decision that it can be shown to enable.
